definitions.explanation: The degree to which something (typically medicine, treatment, or an action) produces the desired result. Often used for tangible, observable effects.

examples.japanese: この{薬|くすり}は{効|き}き{目|め}がある。
{効|き}き{目|め}が{出|で}るまで{時間|じかん}がかかる。
examples.english: It takes time for the effect to appear.

examples.japanese: お{守|まも}りの{効|き}き{目|め}を{信|しん}じて{試験|しけん}に{臨|のぞ}んだ。
examples.english: I went into the exam believing in the power of my good-luck charm.

notes:
Composed of {効|き}く (to work, to be effective) + {目|め} (result, appearance). Most commonly used with medicine, remedies, and treatments, but also applies to charms, strategies, and other actions where one hopes for a tangible result.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {効|き}き{目|め}がある — to be effective, to have an effect
- {効|き}き{目|め}がない — to have no effect
- {効|き}き{目|め}が{出|で}る — the effect appears/kicks in
- {効|き}き{目|め}が{薄|うす}い — the effect is weak
- {効|き}き{目|め}{抜群|ばつぐん} — outstandingly effective

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {効果|こうか} — effect, result; more formal, used in scientific and official contexts
- {効能|こうのう} — efficacy; formal, often seen on medicine labels
- {効力|こうりょく} — effectiveness, potency; formal, often legal or regulatory
